# Compares spending distributions across different education levels
education_order = df.groupby('Education')['Total_Spending'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index

axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('') # Avoid redundant y-label
axes[0, 1].get_yaxis().set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: format(int(x), ',')))

# Shows the density of customers based on their spending on two major categories
hb = axes[1, 0].hexbin(
    df['MntWines'], df['MntMeatProducts'],
    gridsize=20, cmap='inferno',
    mincnt=1 # only show bins with at least 1 data point
)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Spending Density: Wines vs. Meat Products', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Wine Spending', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Meat Product Spending', fontsize=12)
cb = fig.colorbar(hb, ax=axes[1, 0])
cb.set_label('Number of Customers')

# 4. Purchase Channel Correlation (Heatmap)
# Reveals relationships between different purchasing methods and total spending
corr_cols = ['NumDealsPurchases', 'NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 'Total_Spending']
corr_matrix = df[corr_cols].corr()
mask = np.triu(np.ones_like(corr_matrix, dtype=bool))
sns.heatmap(
    ax=axes[1, 1],
    data=corr_matrix,
    annot=True,
    cmap='coolwarm',
    fmt=".2f",
    linewidths=.5,
    mask=mask,
    annot_kws={"size": 12}
)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Correlation of Purchase Channels and Spending', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xticklabels(axes[1, 1].get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, horizontalalignment='right')

# Final adjustments and saving the figure
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
